systems.name: Six Chord-Sound Category System
systems.summary: Pass organizes all harmonic vocabulary into six chord-sound categories — Seventh, Augmented, Minor, Diminished, Minor Seventh Flat Fifth, and Major/Dominant Alteration forms — which together form the taxonomic spine of the book. Chapter 1 presents the voicing inventory silently as a catalog; Chapter 2 deploys these categories in seven functional harmonic contexts. Traversal between categories is governed by common-tone sustain, chromatic approach motion, and cycle-of-fifths movement. Modification rules govern how members of one category may substitute for or approach members of another: diminished voicings substitute for dominant 7b9 sounds, tritone-substitute dominants resolve to major sounds, and augmented chords connect chromatically into cycle cadences. The ii-V-I and cycle-of-fifths skeletons serve as the underlying armature against which all traversal and substitution operate.

members.name: Seventh Chord Forms
members.summary: Dominant and major seventh voicings; the primary target and origin of cycle progressions and turnarounds.

members.name: Augmented Chord Forms
members.summary: Augmented voicings used as chromatic approach chords resolving into cycle cadences.

members.name: Minor Chord Forms
members.summary: Minor triad and minor seventh voicings; function as ii chords and harmonic color in minor-key passages.

members.name: Diminished Chord Forms
members.summary: Fully diminished voicings treated as mobile approach chords with multiple resolution targets; interchangeable with dominant 7b9 sounds.

members.name: Minor Seventh Flat Fifth (Half-Diminished) Forms
members.summary: Half-diminished voicings; function as iio in minor iio-V7b9 cadences, resolving to dominant and augmented forms.

members.name: Major and Dominant Alteration Forms
members.summary: Altered dominant and major voicings including tritone substitutes and upper-structure alterations; primary tonic-resolution targets.

traversal_rules.name: Common-Tone Lead-Note Sustain
traversal_rules.summary: When moving between any two chord-sound categories, sustain the top voice (lead note) if it is common to both chords, creating smooth voice-leading across the change.

references.quote_excerpt: Try to sustain lead notes from one chord to the next

traversal_rules.name: Chromatic Bass-Line Approach Motion
traversal_rules.summary: Traverse from minor-seventh or augmented members to their resolution targets via chromatic bass-line motion.

references.quote_excerpt: movement in Dm7, resolving into Ab13 to G13
Movement is used chromatically to get to the basic cycle

traversal_rules.name: Cycle-of-Fifths Seventh Movement
traversal_rules.summary: Traverse between seventh-category members by following the cycle of fifths, which serves as the default harmonic armature for seventh-chord passages.

references.quote_excerpt: followed by a cycle seventh movement
chromatically to get to the basic cycle

traversal_rules.name: Diminished Chord Multi-Target Resolution
traversal_rules.summary: A diminished member may resolve to any of several chord targets, allowing free traversal from diminished to multiple destination categories.

references.quote_excerpt: Resolve the last chord in this sequence into any chord

traversal_rules.name: Half-Diminished to Dominant and Augmented Resolution
traversal_rules.summary: Traverse from minor-seventh-flat-fifth members through dominant 7b9 forms to augmented resolution, as in the iio-V7b9-aug cadence.

modification_rules.name: Tritone Substitute for Major-Sound Resolution
modification_rules.summary: A dominant seventh chord may be replaced by its tritone substitute when resolving to a major-sound tonic, with upper voices resolving by half-step.

references.quote_excerpt: G13b5 (or Db7+9b5) which resolves into Cma9

modification_rules.name: Diminished Chord as Dominant 7b9 Substitute
modification_rules.summary: Any diminished voicing may substitute for the dominant 7b9 chord, replacing a seventh-flat-ninth member with a diminished member in the ii-V-I skeleton.

references.quote_excerpt: Use of diminished chords for seventh flat ninth chord movement

modification_rules.name: Substitute Turnaround Replacement
modification_rules.summary: A standard I-VI-II-V turnaround may be replaced by a substitute turnaround sequence back to the dominant, introducing alternate harmonic pathways within a single passage.

modification_rules.name: Augmented Sustained Color into Chromatic Resolution
modification_rules.summary: An augmented voicing may be sustained across multiple beats as a color chord and then resolved chromatically into a cycle cadence, functioning as an approach modification of the dominant.

references.quote_excerpt: first six chords are basically G aug. Movement is used chromatically

systems.name: Chord-Symbol Voice-Order Notation Convention
systems.summary: Pass establishes a proprietary notation rule: the left-to-right order of qualifiers in a chord symbol corresponds directly to the bottom-to-top order of voices in the voicing. For example, D7+9+5 means a D7 core with the raised ninth in the next voice above and the raised fifth on top. This is a small but load-bearing system: without it, the entire Chapter 1 diagram catalog and the passage notation in Chapter 2 cannot be correctly decoded.

members.name: Chord Symbol String
members.summary: A chord symbol such as D7+9+5, where the root and quality come first, followed by extension/alteration qualifiers in ascending voice order.

modification_rules.name: Symbol Qualifier Order Equals Voice Layer Order
modification_rules.summary: Each qualifier appended to a chord symbol designates successive voices from the next available string upward, so that reading the symbol left-to-right maps directly onto the fretboard voicing bottom-to-top.

references.quote_excerpt: order of appearance of notes coincides with the spelling of the chord symbol
